name: Malonic aciduria (malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency)
aliases: combined malonic and methylmalonic aciduria (distinct entity)

reference.source: Scriver's OMMBID / Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics
clinicalPearls: A rare organic aciduria caused by deficiency of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase (MLYCD), which converts malonyl-CoA to acetyl-CoA and regulates fatty acid synthesis and oxidation
Presents in infancy or childhood with developmental delay, hypotonia, seizures and cardiomyopathy
Metabolic decompensation with hypoglycaemia, metabolic acidosis and ketosis can occur, sometimes triggered by fasting or illness
The biochemical hallmark is elevated urinary malonic acid, often with a raised malonic to methylmalonic acid ratio
Cardiomyopathy is an important feature and a major determinant of outcome
Management centres on avoiding fasting, a modified diet and supportive metabolic care; carnitine supplementation may be used adjunctively
Diagnosis is supported by urine organic acids and acylcarnitine profile and confirmed by MLYCD molecular testing
reference.pathophysiology: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase converts malonyl-CoA to acetyl-CoA. Malonyl-CoA both provides substrate for fatty acid synthesis and inhibits carnitine palmitoyltransferase 1, the gatekeeper of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation. Loss of the enzyme causes malonyl-CoA accumulation, which impairs long-chain fatty acid oxidation and disturbs the balance of energy metabolism, particularly in heart and brain. Accumulated malonic acid is excreted in urine, giving the characteristic organic aciduria, while impaired energy supply underlies the cardiomyopathy, neurological features and susceptibility to metabolic crises.
additionalDifferentials: Methylmalonic and other classic organic acidaemias
Fatty acid oxidation disorders with cardiomyopathy and hypoglycaemia
Combined malonic and methylmalonic aciduria (ACSF3-related), a distinct entity
Other causes of infantile hypotonia with developmental delay
additionalInvestigations: Urine organic acids showing elevated malonic acid and the malonic to methylmalonic acid ratio
Blood glucose, blood gas and ketone measurement during illness
redFlags: Acute metabolic decompensation with hypoglycaemia and acidosis
Signs of heart failure from cardiomyopathy
reference.prognosis: Outcome is variable and strongly influenced by the severity of cardiomyopathy; with dietary management and avoidance of fasting, some children stabilise, but significant cardiac or neurological disability can persist.
pitfalls: Confusing malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency with the distinct combined malonic and methylmalonic aciduria
Failing to prevent catabolism during intercurrent illness
Misreading a mildly abnormal organic acid profile without confirmatory genetics
references: Nelson Textbook of Paediatrics, organic acid disorders
